newsitem.title: USA: Intl Alliance to shed hazardous waste operations.
newsitem.headline: Intl Alliance to shed hazardous waste operations.

text.p: International Alliance Services Inc Wednesday said its board decided to divest its hazardous waste operations, which have not produced satisfactory profits for the past three years.

The company cited overcapacity in the hazardous waste industry for the operations' lackluster results. In a statement, the company said it signed a non-binding letter of intent and confidentiality agreement with an unidentified large North American environmental services company and a strategic alliance agreement to complement its insurance and surety bond program from its many U.S. facilities.
A company spokesman was not available to elaborate.
A price was not disclosed in the release.

The statement said proceeds from this divestiture, which is expected to be completed during the first half of 1997, will be redeployed into its niche market insurance and outsourcing business services fields.

The company also reported results from continued operations after giving effect to the divestiture of the hazardous waste services business for the year ended December 31, 1996. Net income increased to $4.4 million from $3.5 million in 1995 on increased revenue of $35.8 million as compared with $31 million in 1995.

Although the weighted average number of common and common share equivalents almost doubled to 32.2 million shares from 17 million shares, primary earnings per share were $0.21 compared with $0.20 for 1995 and fully diluted earnings per share were $0.16 in 1996 as compared with $0.20 in 1995. The rise in the number of common shares outstanding during 1996 reflects the private placement with MGD Holdings Ltd of Bermuda and H. Wayne Huizenga of Fort Lauderdale and the year end private placement with several institutional and other accredited investors which raised over $37 million in net proceeds, it said.
